anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level statements or transaction scopes are written in a way that forces the engine to touch more data, rows, or time than business logic really needs.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same resources, causing prolonged blocking or deadlocks within the lock manager.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupted, breaking the correspondence between stored data and its indexes.

When all three root causes co-exist, the database exhibits a multi-layer failure pattern: ill-formed queries and over-long transactions magnify the number and duration of lock acquisitions; corrupted pages or broken index chains make ordinary lookups fall back to broader scans or trigger repeated lock retries, further extending lock hold times. The engine’s monitoring surfaces show a mixture of symptoms—spiking statement latency, swollen slow-query lists, escalating lock-wait and deadlock counts, diverging row counts between index and heap scans, checksum or page-corruption errors, and waves of application timeouts followed by retries that compound the congestion.

Causally, bad workload logic initiates oversized scans and keeps transactions open, inflating the lock footprint and creating hotspots. These longer-running locks increase the probability and depth of blocking chains. Simultaneously, underlying page or index corruption forces the optimizer and storage engine to abandon efficient access paths or to attempt page repairs, adding extra I/O and lock revalidation steps that stall holders and waiters alike. The resulting feedback loop—inefficient queries → extended locks → heightened contention → corruption-induced rescans/rollbacks → even longer transactions—can rapidly degrade throughput, exhaust connection pools, and jeopardize data consistency as forced rollbacks meet structural corruption.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the timeout in seconds for attempts to acquire metadata locks.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_wait_timeout while attempting to acquire a metadata lock.
entry.workload_impact: The metadata lock acquisition fails and the statement does not proceed.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
